# SintBot — full documentation

> SintBot is a free, open-source personal AI agent on your own Mac. Message it in Slack, Feishu or WeCom and it works with Claude Code or Codex, alone or in a team channel.

Generated from https://sintbot.com/ and its guide pages by scripts/build-zh.mjs, with the same text as the pages. Summary: https://sintbot.com/llms.txt

## Key facts

- Cost: free and open source, with no paid tier and no SintBot account. The only costs are the model plans or API keys you choose.
- License: PolyForm Shield 1.0.0 (https://polyformproject.org/licenses/shield/1.0.0).
- Runs on: Apple silicon Macs with macOS 12 or later; needs an installed, signed-in Claude Code or Codex.
- Chat platforms: Slack channels and direct messages, Feishu groups, WeCom groups and direct chats; or a local conversation in the app with no chat account.
- Models: Claude through Claude Code, GPT through Codex; GLM, MiniMax, DeepSeek, Kimi and other services through compatible endpoints and your own API keys.
- Install (recommended, desktop app 0.1.5): download https://github.com/sintlab/sintbot-desktop/releases/latest/download/SintBot_0.1.5_aarch64.dmg, move SintBot to Applications and open it. The app includes the SintBot service and Node.js.
- Install (terminal, needs Node.js 22+): `curl -fsSL https://sintbot.com/install.sh | bash`, then follow https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#terminal
- Current versions: service 1.4.30 (npm package `sintbot`), desktop app 0.1.5.
- Updates: from the console, Settings → Software updates.
- Data: projects, notes and settings are ordinary files on your Mac; chat platforms and model services need a network connection.
- Author WaterTian; publisher SintLab.

## FAQ

### What is SintBot?

A coding assistant that connects a project group to Claude Code or Codex on your own machine. Give it tasks in the group, choose the agent and model, and keep project files and saved notes together.

### Which chat platforms can I use?

SintBot connects to Slack channels and direct messages, Feishu groups and WeCom chats. Each conversation binds to a project, with progress and results returned in the conversation.

### How do teams manage projects?

Bind each group to its own project directory and configure its agent, model and permissions. Use the console to review group status, running tasks, queues and schedules.

### Does everything work offline?

No. SintBot and the project run on your machine, but the chat platform and configured model services require a network connection. Model requests follow the selected agent’s configuration and the service provider’s data policy.

### What do I need to install it?

An Apple silicon Mac running macOS 12 or later and an installed, signed-in Claude Code or Codex. The desktop app includes Node.js. Local conversations need no chat account. Slack needs a workspace where you can install an app (a free one works); connecting Feishu needs a China team identity and phone confirmation. Terminal installation requires Node.js 22+.

### Which models can SintBot use?

Use Claude through Claude Code, GPT through Codex, or add DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or MiniMax to Claude Code with your own API key: pick the preset, paste the key, then choose the model for each group. Other compatible services can use custom endpoints.

### What stays when I switch models?

Project files and saved shared notes remain. Switching starts a fresh conversation; record decisions and unfinished work in the project so the next agent can read them and continue.

### Is SintBot free?

Yes. SintBot is free and open source, with no paid tier and no SintBot account to create. It works through the Claude Code or Codex you already use, so the only costs are the model plans or API keys you choose. Projects, notes and settings stay as ordinary files on your Mac, and updates install from the console.

Source: https://sintbot.com/guide/install/

## Install SintBot on your Mac

Download the desktop app, move it to Applications and open it. Connect Slack, Feishu or WeCom, or start with a local conversation.

macOS · Node.js included · Codex / Claude Code · Slack · Feishu · WeCom

[Install the desktop app](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#desktop) [Connect Slack](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#slack)

Also supported: [Feishu](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#feishu) · [WeCom](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#wecom)

### Three steps to your first task

For Apple silicon Macs running macOS 12 or later. App 0.1.5 includes SintBot and Node.js; no separate Node.js or npm installation is needed. Install and sign in to Codex or Claude Code first.

[Download for Mac](https://github.com/sintlab/sintbot-desktop/releases/latest/download/SintBot_0.1.5_aarch64.dmg)

#### 01 Move SintBot to Applications

Open the downloaded DMG. Drag SintBot on the left to Applications on the right, then open SintBot from Applications. You can eject the disk image afterwards.

#### 02 Choose a project and connection

On first launch, the App prepares its local service and opens setup. Name your project and choose Codex or Claude Code. Under Chat platform the English page lists Slack first: create your own Slack app from a link that is already filled in, paste two tokens, then send the bot one message. [Connect Slack](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#slack) below has each step.

Feishu and WeCom are also supported. Pick “飞书 · Feishu” there to scan with a Feishu China team identity and connect a project group, or “企业微信 · WeCom” to scan with WeCom and create a bot; see [Feishu](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#feishu) or [WeCom](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#wecom) below. To start locally instead, choose “Use on this Mac first” and connect Slack later.

#### 03 Send your first task

Use Chat for local conversations, or the Slack conversation you connected (@mention the bot in a channel). With Feishu, use the new project group; with WeCom, the chat you connected. Ask “Read the first line of README.md and reply with that line only”, then compare the reply with your file. The screen below shows where to enter a local task.

**Desktop installation is complete**

Open SintBot from Applications or the menu bar next time. No repeated scan or open terminal is needed. Continue to the [usage guide](https://sintbot.com/guide/usage/) for models, follow-ups and updates.

##### Close the window, quit or stop?

Closing the window leaves the App in the menu bar. Quitting the App leaves the bot running. Choose “Stop SintBot and Quit” to stop both. A service installed by the App stays stopped until Start or the next App launch. An adopted service keeps its original login settings.

“Remove Background Service” preserves settings and history; it does not delete your project.

##### How do the App and service update?

Upgrade the service in Settings → Software updates. A managed service waits for tasks to settle before switching, and rolls back if reconnection fails. To update the App itself, download the new DMG, quit the App and replace it in Applications. An existing SintBot service is reused; avoid installing a second instance.

##### Setup did not open on first launch?

Check the App status page. An existing service opens its console directly. If an executor is missing, install and sign in to Codex or Claude Code, then retry. Open the log from the menu bar for the specific error.

The official DMG is signed and Apple notarized. If the download is damaged or cannot be verified, download it again from the official release. Keep system security protections enabled.

### Connect your project to Slack

Choose a project on your Mac, create your own Slack app from a link that is already filled in, paste two tokens, then send the bot one message. SintBot connects over Socket Mode, so you need no public address, and a free workspace works.

1. **01**Create app
2. **02**Two tokens
3. **03**One message
4. **04**First task

**Before you start**

Have Codex or Claude Code working on your Mac. You need permission to install apps in the Slack workspace; if yours needs admin approval, create a free workspace of your own. One Slack app serves one Mac.

#### 01 Create the app from the setup page

First launch opens setup. Enter a project name, choose the executor and pick “Slack” under Chat platform. Select “Create app in Slack”: Slack opens with the app’s permissions and events already filled in. Pick your workspace, select Next, then Create. Leave “Declare it as a Slack Agent”, below the button, unticked unless you want Slack’s own Stop button and “Working…” status in channel threads: a declared app cannot be used by workspace guests, every direct message with it becomes a thread, and neither can be undone.

#### 02 Paste the two tokens

1. On the app’s Basic Information page in Slack, scroll to App-Level Tokens, select Generate Token and Scopes, add the `connections:write` scope and generate. Paste the token that starts with `xapp-` into setup; it is checked at once. The app settings page in Slack can take ten seconds or more to load the first time; reload it if it stays blank.
2. Select “Open install page” in setup, then in Slack select the install button named after your workspace (for example Install to Acme), and Allow.
3. Copy the Bot User OAuth Token that starts with `xoxb-`, paste it and select “Connect Slack”.

Both tokens are saved on this Mac only; never post them in a chat. If a token lands in the wrong field, setup says which kind you pasted.

If this Mac reaches Slack only through a proxy (for example on mainland-China networks), enter an `http://` address under “Proxy” in the Slack step; it is filled in for you when the terminal that opened setup has a proxy set. The proxy is saved with the connection, so the background service and the desktop app use it later. It is the network proxy of the whole service, so other chat platforms and the local model tools use it too.

#### 03 Send the bot one message

When setup shows “Waiting for your message…”, select “Open the bot in Slack” and send it any message within 10 minutes. To use a channel instead, invite the bot with `/invite @your-bot-name` and @mention it there.

SintBot binds that conversation to the project, the bot replies “已连接项目 …” (project connected) and setup opens the console.

#### 04 Send your first task

In the same conversation, start with a read-only request:

Send to the bot in Slack (@mention it in a channel)

Read the first line of this project’s README.md and reply with only that line. Do not change any files.

Check the reply against the first line of the file on your Mac. While the task runs your message shows ⏳; it becomes ✅ when the answer arrives. To stop a task, send `!stop` (@mention the bot in a channel). Then continue with [working in Slack](https://sintbot.com/guide/usage/#slack-workflow).

##### Already using Feishu, WeCom or local chat? Add Slack

Open Settings in the console and expand the Slack card (platform cards start collapsed), choose the project folder and executor, then follow the same three steps and send the bot one message. Your existing connections, local chat and projects are kept.

Once connected, the card shows a status dot, the workspace and the number of bound conversations even when collapsed. Expand it, then Advanced, to refresh the connection status or open the app’s settings in Slack.

##### Bind another channel

Invite the bot to the channel with `/invite @your-bot-name`, then pick that channel under Groups · Projects → Set up a group project in the console and choose its folder and executor. Only channels the bot has joined are listed; if you type in the ID of a channel it has not joined, the console tells you to invite it first. One app can serve several projects but connects to only one SintBot.

##### The link does not open?

Create the app by hand: at api.slack.com/apps choose Create New App → From a manifest, pick the workspace and paste the [manifest file](https://github.com/sintlab/sintbot/blob/main/docs/slack-app-manifest.yaml), then continue from step 02. Leave token rotation off: it cannot be turned off again.

##### No reply to your message?

In a channel, @mention the bot and check it was invited; when SintBot says the bot is not in the channel, send `/invite @your-bot-name` there, and invite it again after reinstalling the app. Check the connection status under Settings → Slack: if it shows Disconnected, check the network or proxy; if it shows a failed connection, a token was revoked or the app was removed (shown within about 5 minutes), so connect again with new tokens. If this Mac reaches Slack only through a proxy, enter it under “Proxy” in the Slack step of setup and try again; for an installation already in use, set `proxy` in the configuration file (for example `{"https": "http://127.0.0.1:7890"}`) and restart the service. Make sure no other SintBot uses the same app: Slack hands each message to only one of an app’s connections. If another machine seems to be using it, the Slack connection in the console turns yellow with a warning. If more than 10 minutes passed during setup without a message, select Retry on the setup page.

### Connect your project to Feishu

Choose a project on your Mac, confirm on your phone, then send a task in the new group. Desktop and terminal installations share this setup flow.

1. **01**Project
2. **02**Confirm
3. **03**Create group
4. **04**First task

**Before you scan**

Have Codex or Claude Code working on your Mac. Sign in to Feishu China on your phone with an enterprise or team identity; create or join a team first if needed. Your organization may require administrator approval.

#### 01 Choose your project on the Mac

First launch opens setup. Enter a project name, choose the executor and pick “飞书 · Feishu” under Chat platform. Use the new project folder or expand “Use an existing project folder”. Select “Connect Feishu”.

If you are not an organization administrator, expand “Organization options” and select “I am not an organization administrator”. An administrator will need to finish app availability and publication.

#### 02 Confirm with Feishu on your phone

Keep setup open on your Mac. Use the scanner in the Feishu mobile app to scan the code on your own setup page.

1. Check the enterprise or team selected on your phone.
2. Review the app’s team and requested permissions.
3. Confirm on your phone, then return to your Mac.

These images show setup states. The pictured code is for this walkthrough; use the fresh code on your own Mac to connect.

#### 03 Wait for the app and group

SintBot creates the app, checks permissions, creates a project group and saves configuration. Keep the window open. Expand “Connection details” to follow progress; setup opens the console when complete.

#### 04 Send a task in the new group

Find the newly created project group in Feishu and check that SintBot is a member. Start with a read-only request:

Send to your new Feishu project group

Read the first line of this project’s README.md and reply with that line only. Do not change any files.

Compare the reply with the file on your Mac. A correct reply verifies the group, executor and project path together. Continue with the [Feishu group workflow](https://sintbot.com/guide/usage/#feishu-workflow).

##### Confirmed on your phone, but no new group?

If setup asks for a group, create one in Feishu, add the newly created bot, then paste the group ID into setup and select “Continue”. An ID starts with `oc_…`; it is not a group name or invitation link. Ask an administrator to finish publication and availability if the app is not available to you.

For other failures, use “Retry” or “Edit details” as prompted. A successfully connected project needs no repeated scan.

##### Already using local conversations?

An existing configuration opens the console directly. To add Feishu, let tasks finish, stop the service, run `sintbot connect --attach` and complete the scan, then start again. Configuration, records and local conversations are kept. The current console has no one-click attach action. See [terminal installation and maintenance](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#terminal).

##### Connected, but the group gets no reply?

Check Settings → Feishu for connection status and Groups · Projects for the target group, folder and model. Confirm the bot is a member, the app is published, and message permissions and event subscriptions are enabled. Mention the bot if your group requires it.

### Connect your project to WeCom

Choose a project on your Mac, scan with WeCom on your phone to create a bot, then send it one message. SintBot receives tasks over a long connection, so you need no public callback URL and no group.

1. **01**Project
2. **02**Scan
3. **03**One message
4. **04**First task

**Before you scan**

Have Codex or Claude Code working on your Mac. Install WeCom on your phone and join or create an organization. Creating one is free and needs no verification; an organization with only you in it works too.

#### 01 Choose your project on the Mac

First launch opens setup. Enter a project name, choose the executor, pick “企业微信 · WeCom” under Chat platform and select “Scan to create bot”. Use the new project folder or expand “Use an existing project folder”.

#### 02 Scan with WeCom on your phone

Keep setup open on your Mac and scan the code on your own page with the WeCom scanner on your phone.

1. Check which organization is selected on your phone.
2. Confirm creating the bot. It is named after you by default.
3. The Bot ID and Secret are saved on this Mac. There is nothing to copy; never send them in a chat.

These images show interface states, and the code is for illustration only. Scan the new code on your own Mac; an expired code is replaced automatically.

#### 03 Send the bot one message

When setup shows “Waiting for your message…”, send the bot any message in WeCom within 10 minutes: message it directly, or add it to a group and @mention it. Find it by searching its name at the top of WeCom, or under Workbench → Smart Bots.

SintBot binds that chat to the project, the bot replies “已连接项目 …” (project connected) and setup opens the console.

#### 04 Send your first task

In the same chat, start with a read-only request:

Send to the WeCom bot (@mention it in a group)

Read the first line of this project’s README.md and reply with only that line. Do not change any files.

Check the reply against the first line of the file on your Mac. The bot replies when a task finishes; progress is not shown while it runs. Then continue with [working in WeCom](https://sintbot.com/guide/usage/#wecom-workflow).

##### Already using Feishu or local chat? Add WeCom

Open Settings in the console and expand the WeCom card (platform cards start collapsed), choose the project folder and executor, select “Scan to create bot”, then send the bot one message as above. Your Feishu connection, local chat and projects are kept.

Once connected, the card shows a status dot, the bot’s name and the number of bound conversations even when collapsed. Expand it, then Advanced, for the Bot ID and to refresh the connection status.

##### Already have a bot? Enter Bot ID and Secret manually

Expand “Already have a bot? Enter Bot ID and Secret” on the setup page, or Advanced on the console’s WeCom card, enter the existing bot’s Bot ID and Secret, then send the bot one message. To create a bot manually, use either entry below, choose API mode and select “Use long connection”:

- WeCom desktop: Workbench → Smart Bots → Create bot → Manual creation.
- Admin console at work.weixin.qq.com: Security & Management → Management Tools → Smart Bots.

##### Bind another project

Create a WeCom group, add the bot and @mention it once, then pick that group under Groups · Projects → Set up a group project in the console and choose its folder and executor. One bot can serve several projects but connects to only one SintBot.

##### No reply to your message?

Check the connection status under Settings → WeCom. If it shows Disconnected, select Refresh connection status, check the network and make sure no other SintBot or tool is using this bot: each bot keeps only one connection at a time. In groups, @mention the bot; @All does not trigger it. If more than 10 minutes passed during setup without a message, select Retry on the setup page.

##### Alternative: terminal installation and maintenance

### Prepare your project Mac

The terminal steps below are for **SintBot 1.4.30** on macOS with Node.js 22 or later and Codex or Claude Code. Start with local conversations, or connect 1–32 project conversations: Slack direct messages or channels, with Feishu China groups and WeCom chats or groups also supported. The desktop App includes Node.js.

- You can start with the automatically created project folder or choose an existing project on this Mac.
- Node.js is version 22 or later.
- Codex or Claude Code (at least one) is installed, signed in and working in your local terminal.
- For Slack, you can install apps in the workspace; a free workspace you create yourself works. Feishu needs a team identity in Feishu on your phone, and WeCom a scan with WeCom.

##### How do I check my environment?

Terminal

```
node --version
codex --version
claude --version
```

Node.js and the runner you use should report a version before you continue. Keep using your existing Codex or Claude Code installation and account.

##### What if a version check fails?

If a command cannot be found, finish installing that tool and open a new terminal. Get Node.js from its [official website](https://nodejs.org/en/download); follow the official instructions for your chosen coding agent to install it and sign in. The SintBot installer installs SintBot itself.

### Install SintBot in one command

Copy this into your local terminal. The installer checks the environment, installs the package and verifies the result.

Terminal

```
curl -fsSL https://sintbot.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Installation complete**

When you see `Installed and verified SintBot 1.4.30`, installation is complete. Continue with the project and chat platform setup.

##### Optional: preview the installation plan

To inspect the plan before installing, use this command instead. It downloads no package and changes no configuration. Then run the installation command above.

Terminal

```
curl -fsSL https://sintbot.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --dry-run
```

##### Optional: check the version and help

Terminal

```
SINTBOT="$HOME/.local/share/sintbot/bin/sintbot"
"$SINTBOT" --version
"$SINTBOT" help
```

SintBot is installed in `~/.local/share/sintbot`. Continue below to connect your project to Slack, Feishu or WeCom.

### Open local setup

Run this command. On the English setup page, Slack is listed first and already selected under Chat platform: follow the [Slack walkthrough](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#slack) to create the app, paste two tokens and send the bot one message. Feishu and WeCom are also supported: pick “飞书 · Feishu” or “企业微信 · WeCom” there and follow the [Feishu](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#feishu) or [WeCom](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#wecom) walkthrough. You can also choose “Use on this Mac first”.

```
"$HOME/.local/share/sintbot/bin/sintbot" start --ui
```

### Choose the project on the setup page

By default setup creates `~/Projects/sintbot` with a README and binds it to the conversation you connect. To connect an existing project, enter its absolute path in the existing-project field; the directory must exist. Do not use your entire home directory as a project. Afterwards, manage project folders and models under Groups · Projects in the console.

##### Prefer the terminal?

For Feishu, the same flow runs as `sintbot connect`; `--name`, `--workdir`, `--provider` and `--basic` map to the options on the page. See the full install guide.

### Everyday start

When setup completes the service is already running; there is nothing else to run. Every later start uses the same command:

Terminal

```
"$HOME/.local/share/sintbot/bin/sintbot" start --ui
```

Keep the terminal open. Settings shows the Slack, Feishu and WeCom connection status; Groups · Projects manages bindings. Public console access and administrator sign-in are optional.

##### The console shows “Needs attention”?

After a power loss or forced restart during a task, the service holds the groups whose result is unknown and lists them on the overview’s “Needs attention” card; the service still starts when every group is held, so the console stays available. Two cases usually no longer hold a group: Claude Code, or Codex with busy follow-ups off, reporting an error before it starts (the group is told why; Codex groups with busy follow-ups on, the default, keep the previous behaviour in this release), and a service crash that interrupts a running task (the group is told, and the task is not redone). While an upgrade is still confirming the new version, up to 90 seconds after the switch, an error before starting still holds the group so that a rollback stays safe. When the background service supports automatic restart and the other groups are idle and settled, click “Seal and continue”: the record is archived unchanged, that message is not processed again, and the service restarts by itself with a new record; resend the message if needed. In a foreground run, seal from a terminal as described in the [full install guide](https://github.com/sintlab/sintbot/blob/main/docs/install.md).

**Restart an existing installation directly**

Do not repeat setup (Slack tokens or a scan) or initialize again for a normal restart. If you used `--config` or `--data-dir`, pass the same flags on every start.

### Verify with a real message

Send this in the conversation you just connected: the Slack direct message (in a channel, @mention the bot), the Feishu group or the WeCom chat:

> Read the first line of this project’s README.md and reply with only that line.

Compare the reply with the file. This checks the chat connection, the runner and the project path together.

#### Commands and console

In a Feishu group, any text message is a task; the reply card appears once the model starts, or after 25 seconds if it is still working without output. While it runs, the card shows how long it has run, what it is doing and the steps already delivered, which fold into a Process section at the end. These commands are answered at once and never take a task slot:

- **`/status`**: Model, project, busy or idle (steps and current work while busy), and queue.

- **`/skip`**: Cancel only the current task; queued messages run next and the conversation is kept.

- **`/stop`**: Stop the current task and cancel queued ones; the conversation is kept.

- **`/new`**: Start a new conversation, forgetting the previous one, while the group is idle.

- **`/model`**: Opens a tap-to-pick card: choose the backend, model and thinking depth, then confirm. You can also send `/model high`, `/model <model>` or `/model <backend>`. A model or depth change continues the conversation; a backend change starts a new one. Only while the group is idle.

- **`/hud`**: Quota of the current model and usage of this conversation.

- **`/issue text`**: Log feedback for the console.

- **`/help`**: List commands, with this group's project and model.

Send a command as a message of its own; except for `/issue` and `/model`, add no other text. If the Feishu app subscribes to the message-recall event, recalling your own message cancels it.

In Slack, commands start with `!` instead of `/`, because Slack keeps `/` for itself: `!status`, `!stop`, `!skip`, `!new`, `!model` and `!help`. In a channel, @mention the bot with the command. Your message shows ⏳ while the task runs and ✅ when the answer arrives; the [Slack walkthrough](https://sintbot.com/guide/slack/) covers everyday use. In WeCom, @mention the bot in a group for every task and command.

With `--ui`, open `http://127.0.0.1:4600` on this Mac to see every group, stop tasks, start a new conversation for an idle group, bind new groups, switch the model or project of an idle group, and add or configure models. Set a console password in its settings before enabling LAN access. To add a group without the console, add it to the configuration and restart; it is registered automatically.

Model and thinking depth are chosen per group: on the group card, the Model row picks the backend and model and the next row picks the depth. Codex and Claude lists are read live from the local executors; DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi and MiniMax lists come live from the provider once the model card has an API key. Those cards keep only the connection and key and have no model field (a custom endpoint still asks for its model name); a group that has not chosen runs the card’s default.

Model settings are grouped into model and reasoning, context and compaction, and connection; on a DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or MiniMax card, everything except the API key and name sits under Advanced. For Codex, choose the executor default or a custom context window; known limits are checked on save. Compaction also offers default or custom, with numeric inputs shown only when needed. Codex uses a threshold and Claude Code a compaction window; either may compact earlier. Existing explicit global values become independent settings on existing models. Changes apply to the next turn and preserve the session. Capacity details distinguish requested settings from runtime reports.

For Claude Code groups, SintBot can compact the current session between turns when the CLI reports compaction support and the context reaches half of a custom compaction window. It uses a spare concurrency slot and stays silent in the group. A new message interrupts compaction before starting its turn; a window of 0 disables only idle compaction; compaction during a turn follows the executor’s defaults. `/hud` shows the compaction line and last completion time. Claude subscription quota prefers rate-limit events reported by the executor.

#### Stop and restart

In the running terminal, press `Ctrl` + `C` and wait for the process to exit. Keep the configuration from setup and use the same start command:

Terminal

```
SINTBOT="$HOME/.local/share/sintbot/bin/sintbot"
"$SINTBOT" start --ui
```

Use `start` for normal restarts. Do not run `init` again.

##### The bot does not reply

Check the terminal error first. In Slack, @mention the bot in a channel and check that it has been invited (`/invite @your-bot-name`); the [Slack walkthrough](https://sintbot.com/guide/slack/) lists the other cases. In Feishu, verify that the application is published, the bot has joined the target group, message permissions and event subscriptions are configured, the credentials are valid and the project group is bound. A successful preflight does not prove that the chat platform accepts the credentials or delivers messages.

##### A group is paused or startup reports unresolved receipts

When a group's last result cannot be confirmed, only that group is held and the console stays available. Check what the task actually did. If the console offers “Seal and continue”, use it to archive the record unchanged and restart the service. Otherwise stop the service, run `sintbot incident seal --group <group ID>` and start again. Do not clear logs, overwrite unknown outcomes or blindly resend the task.

USAGE GUIDE

## Your first task on your Mac

Open the desktop App and give a task locally, in Slack, or in a Feishu or WeCom chat. Choose a project and model, review the result and continue.

[Start with your first message](https://sintbot.com/guide/usage/#first-task)

Start with the [desktop installation guide](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#desktop), then [connect Slack](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#slack) or choose a local conversation. [Feishu](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#feishu) and [WeCom](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#wecom) are also supported. Existing installations do not need to connect again.

APP

### Your desktop workspace

Open Chat to give a local task. Groups · Projects selects the folder, model and thinking depth. Models · Library manages accounts and API keys. Settings holds the interface language, the Slack, Feishu and WeCom connections and software updates. Start with a read-only task, then adjust execution permissions as needed.

Local conversations need no Slack, Feishu or WeCom account. To work in Slack, connect it first; Feishu and WeCom connect by scanning with your phone. Every route uses the same project and model settings.

### Start working in Slack

Finish the [Slack setup walkthrough](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#slack) first. In a direct message, every message is a task and the answer arrives in the conversation. In a channel, @mention the bot; the answer arrives in a thread under your message, and to follow up you @mention it again in that thread. Start with a small task to confirm the project, then continue with longer ones.

- Commands start with `!`, because Slack keeps `/` for its own commands: `!status`, `!stop`, `!skip`, `!new`, `!model` and `!help`. Outside threads, `/sint stop` and the other commands also work.
- While a task runs, your message shows ⏳; it becomes ✅ when the answer arrives. Progress text is not shown while it runs.
- The bot’s own notices and command replies are in English in Slack. To switch a conversation to Chinese, open its card in the console and choose the notice language under More settings; the model still answers in the language you write to it.
- To stop a task, say stop where the task is. In the task’s thread, @mention the bot with `!stop`: only that thread’s task stops, and queued tasks still run. To stop the whole channel, the current task and everything queued, @mention the bot with `!stop` as a new message in the channel, or use `/sint stop` there. In a direct message, just send `!stop`. Apps declared as a Slack Agent also show Slack’s own Stop button in channel threads; it does the same as `!stop` typed in that thread.
- A task that could not finish, for example because the service was stopped mid-way, gets ⚠️ instead of ⏳, and its thread says it did not finish. SintBot never runs it again by itself; send it again if you still need it.
- In a channel, each thread is its own task. While a task runs, a message in its thread (@mention the bot there) joins that task once the model reads it; it gets ⏳ too, and the answer arrives in that thread. A new @mention outside that thread waits as a task of its own: its thread says it is queued, and the answer arrives in its own thread. At most two messages wait; beyond that the bot asks you to send again once the current task is done. In a direct message, a message sent while a task runs joins it. To make every message wait instead of joining, turn off busy follow-ups for that project in the console. `!skip` drops the current task and continues with the queue.
- Send images and files together with the task; they are saved on your Mac for the task to read. Files over 30 MB are not downloaded.
- Deleting your message cancels it: a waiting message is dropped and a running task stops.
- The task cannot send files into Slack yet; the answer names the file’s path in the project. Long answers arrive as several consecutive messages.

### Start work in your Feishu group

Complete the [Feishu walkthrough](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#feishu) first. In the new project group, ordinary messages are tasks. Mention the bot if your group requires it. Attach files or screenshots to the message and explain what you want done.

Your first task

Read the first line of README.md and reply with that line only. Do not change any files.

#### Check the group and project in the console

Open Groups · Projects, find the group and check its project folder, executor, model and thinking depth. Each group has its own project. Verify these before asking for file changes.

#### Follow progress

Read the reply card in the same group. Send `/status` to check activity and the queue.

#### Add instructions

Send a follow-up while the task runs. It joins the current turn when available, or waits in the queue.

#### Stop or start fresh

`/stop` stops the task and clears queued messages. Use `/new` while idle for a new conversation.

Closing the desktop window leaves the bot running. Keep the Mac on and connected, with the SintBot service running, to continue sending tasks from Feishu.

### Start working in WeCom

Finish the [WeCom setup walkthrough](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#wecom) first. In a direct chat, send tasks without a mention. In a group, @mention the bot for every task or group command; @All does not trigger it. Start with a small task to confirm the project, then continue with longer tasks. The bot replies when a task finishes; progress is not shown while it runs.

- Send files and images directly in a direct chat. In groups, the bot receives only text and messages that mix text and images: send images together with text, and put files in the project folder first or send them in a direct chat.
- Ask the assistant to send project files and images back to the current chat. Size limits follow WeCom’s rules.
- Use /status for status and /stop to stop a task. Recalling a message does not stop it.
- Group history queries, editing, recall and reactions are unavailable. Do not automatically resend an unconfirmed delivery.

01

### Start with a small task

Use local Chat or the group connected to your project. Start with a read-only request whose answer you can check against a local file.

Your first message

```
Read the first line of this project’s README and reply with that line. Do not change any files.
```

1. **Send the request**Write it in the configured project group. If your setup requires mentions, mention the bot.
2. **Follow the response**SintBot works in the bound project directory and returns progress and the final reply to the same conversation.
3. **Check the result**Compare the reply with your README. This checks the full path from group message to agent and back.

Before the first message, complete the [installation and connection steps](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/). A successful package installation alone does not verify a model turn.

02

### Define the task and success criteria

Include the outcome, the relevant context, what should stay unchanged and what a completed result looks like. Attach a screenshot or file when it carries information that words cannot.

A useful development brief

```
Improve the homepage navigation on phones.
Keep the current fonts, colors and desktop layout.
Use the attached screenshot to locate the issue.
Check widths of 390 px and 768 px, then send a screenshot and explain what changed.
```

##### When you want an investigation first

Ask for the cause, affected files and a proposed fix before editing. For example: “Find why the sign-in button fails. Read the relevant code and logs, then explain the cause and the smallest fix.”

##### When you want it to make the change

State that it can edit, name the intended behavior and give a checkable outcome. Mention any files or behavior it should preserve.

##### When a task has several parts

List the deliverables in order and identify dependencies. State which parts can be handled independently and how their results should be checked together.

03

### Review results in the group

Progress and the final result return to the project conversation. Depending on the task, the result may be an explanation, changed files, an image, a report or a preview.

1. **Read the outcome**Check what changed, how it was checked and whether any part still needs a decision.
2. **Inspect the artifact**Open the delivered file or preview. For code, inspect the changes in the project and run the checks appropriate to the work.
3. **Give precise feedback**Point to a section, file, screenshot or behavior. Say what should change and what is already right.

A focused follow-up

```
The phone layout is right. Keep it.
Make the active navigation item easier to see, using the existing accent color.
Send an updated screenshot after checking the same two widths.
```

**While a task is running in 1.4.30**

Send additional instructions directly in the project group. Busy follow-ups are on by default for Claude Code and Codex; they queue when disabled or unavailable. “Joined” means the model has read the message, and long-running tools can delay that step.

The console’s Message action also works while a group is busy. It follows the group’s follow-up setting: the message waits for model reading or joins the queue. “Accepted” does not yet confirm that the model has read it. Start a new session or switch models only after the group is idle.

04

### Choose an agent, then its model

The coding agent executes the work. Its configured model service handles the model requests. These are two separate choices.

| Coding agent | Model or service | Configuration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Claude | Your Claude Code account and configuration |
| Claude Code | DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax | A preset in the model library and your own API key |
| Claude Code | Another compatible service | A custom compatible endpoint |
| Codex | GPT | Your Codex account and model configuration |

Use the project’s model configuration to choose the route and model. Keep provider keys in local configuration; do not post them in the group. Available choices follow the agent and accounts configured on the machine.

**Before switching**

Ask SintBot to record decisions and unfinished work in the project. Switching the backend starts a fresh conversation; changing the model or thinking depth on the same backend continues it. Saved files and shared notes remain either way.

Before scanning, SintBot reads the selected executor’s live model list and saves its recommended model and thinking depth for the new group. The setup page shows the selected values; you can change them later in Groups · Projects. If the live recommendation is unavailable, setup stops before creating a new app: check the executor’s login and network, then retry. Existing group choices are preserved.

Model and thinking depth are chosen per group: change them on the console’s group card, or send `/model` in the group for a tap-to-pick card and confirm; text such as `/model high` also works. Either needs the group to be idle.

**Codex speed (Fast).** Codex models have a Speed option: Standard or Fast, Standard by default. Three ways to turn it on: send `/model fast` in the group (`/model standard` to go back); the `/model` card gains a Speed row, pick then confirm as usual; the console group card gains a Speed dropdown. Changing only the speed never resets the session, works while a task is running and applies from the next message. It is remembered per group and per model card: Fast on GPT in one group does not affect that group’s other models. Only models with a Fast tier can turn it on; otherwise the request is refused and nothing changes, and switching to a model without it returns to Standard with a note. The receipt states the cost: the model is unchanged, requests are queued at a higher priority, about 1.5–2x faster depending on the model, and included subscription usage is charged at 2.5x (purchased credits at 2x). When Fast is off, every turn explicitly asks for standard speed. When App Server explicitly reports a fallback, the card footer omits Fast. Older executors and the exec route may not report the effective tier; a Fast label alone is not proof that acceleration took effect.

**API-key models.** In Models · Library choose Add model, pick DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or MiniMax, paste your own API key (Verify key runs a short test) and name the card; the endpoint and other details are under Advanced. The card has no model field: once the key is in, pick the model and thinking depth per group in Groups · Projects from the provider’s live list. The model library includes a DeepSeek card, selectable even before a key is entered; its preset model is `deepseek-flash[1m]`. Without a key, the turn is refused before it starts with “this model card has no API key yet”; no other credentials are borrowed.

Model settings are grouped into model and reasoning, context and compaction, and connection; on a DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or MiniMax card, everything except the API key and name sits under Advanced. For Codex, choose the executor default or a custom context window; known limits are checked on save. Compaction also offers default or custom, with numeric inputs shown only when needed. Codex uses a threshold and Claude Code a compaction window; either may compact earlier. Existing explicit global values become independent settings on existing models. Changes apply to the next turn and preserve the session. Capacity details distinguish requested settings from runtime reports.

For Claude Code groups, SintBot can compact the current session between turns when the CLI reports compaction support and the context reaches half of a custom compaction window. It uses a spare concurrency slot and stays silent in the group. A new message interrupts compaction before starting its turn; a window of 0 disables only idle compaction; compaction during a turn follows the executor’s defaults. `/hud` shows the compaction line and last completion time. Claude subscription quota prefers rate-limit events reported by the executor.

05

### Save decisions in your project

A conversation is useful while work is in progress. Project notes keep the decisions that the next task or model will need.

- **Project rules:** naming, coding conventions, design choices and verification steps.
- **Current handoff:** what is complete, what is pending and the next concrete action.
- **Useful evidence:** relevant files, confirmed causes and links to decisions.

Ask for a handoff

```
Record today’s decisions, completed work and remaining tasks in the project handoff.
Include the files and checks needed to continue.
Keep it concise and preserve the existing project conventions.
```

Saved notes are shared project context. Unsaved chat details do not automatically become shared memory. Check the handoff before changing models or starting a new session.

06

### Share screenshots, files and previews

Attach a reference to the group and describe how it should guide the work: layout, typography, colors, interaction or a particular component.

##### Build or refine an interface

Name the page or component, specify what to preserve and ask for desktop and phone checks. Review the delivered screenshot before opening the interactive preview.

##### Generate or revise an image

State the image’s purpose and the changes you want. When the existing image matters, provide it as the reference and identify the parts to keep.

##### Review an annotated design

Attach an annotated screenshot to the group and keep revisions in the project. Refer to a specific image or comment when requesting the next version.

##### Continue after browser sign-in

If a browser task needs your sign-in or verification, open the takeover entry sent to the group, complete the step yourself and tell SintBot to continue. Do not send passwords or verification codes in the conversation.

07

### Manage everyday project work

**Desktop start, stop and updates**

Open SintBot from Applications or the menu bar. Closing the window or quitting the App keeps the service running. Choose “Stop SintBot and Quit” to stop it. Upgrade the service in Settings → Software updates; its Release notes link opens this site’s [changelog](https://sintbot.com/changelog/). The Claude subscription card’s settings in Models · Library show the installed Claude Code version and offer an upgrade while no Claude Code group is running or queued. From 0.1.4 the App checks for its own updates, asks before installing, then reopens while the service keeps running; choose Check for Updates… in the menu to check now. Versions up to 0.1.3 have to be replaced once with a new DMG.

Keep a clear boundary between the project, the people giving it work and the permissions available to the agent.

#### Project groups

Each group is bound to its project. The console overview shows concurrency, group state, configured reasoning effort and the latest context usage. Select a group to view tasks, then expand replies, tools and usage. Row icons provide message, stop and new-session controls.

#### Permissions

Begin with read-only requests. The project administrator chooses the permissions required for editing files and running commands.

#### Scheduled tasks

On a group card in the console, open More settings → Scheduled tasks. At the set time SintBot can hand a task to the agent, post a reminder or run a command in the project folder, once or on a schedule. Each due time runs at most once, and a run missed while the service was off is not made up. WeCom chats do not have scheduled tasks yet.

#### Model services

Project files stay on the machine; chat messages and model requests use the configured external services. Account terms and usage limits apply.

##### Starting and stopping the 1.4.30 foreground installation

Keep the terminal running while you use the connected group. Press Ctrl-C and wait for shutdown to finish. For a normal restart, use the same start command from the installation guide; do not rerun initialization.

To upgrade, check Settings → Software updates in the console, then press Ctrl-C, rerun the one-line installer and start with the same command. If your own launchd agent runs SintBot, Upgrade now in the console installs the new version and switches over once every group is idle, and restores the previous version if the new one does not connect.

If a group is paused or startup reports unresolved receipts, preserve the state and inspect what happened, then restart or seal that group as the installation guide describes. Do not delete the journal or repeat a task blindly.

[Open the start and verification steps →](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/#start)

### Ready to connect a project?

The installation guide takes you from the local package to a verified group reply.

[Open installation guide](https://sintbot.com/guide/install/)

Platform walkthroughs: [Slack](https://sintbot.com/guide/slack/) · [Feishu](https://sintbot.com/guide/feishu/) · [WeCom](https://sintbot.com/guide/wecom/)


Source: https://sintbot.com/changelog/

CHANGELOG

## What changed in each release

Every SintBot release from 1.4.1 to 1.4.30, newest first, with the notes published for that version.

[Latest release: 1.4.30](https://sintbot.com/changelog/#v1.4.30)

2026-11-20

### 1.4.30 · Fewer held groups, models chosen per group, a tidier console

- **A start that fails at once no longer holds the group**: When Claude Code, or Codex in a group with Add follow-up messages to the current task turned off, reports an error before it starts on a message (for example the usage limit is reached, the sign-in has expired, the previous session cannot be resumed, the chosen model is not available, or the model service cannot be reached), the message is closed as not handled: the conversation is told why and asked to send it again later, and the group keeps handling new messages. Before, this held the whole group, and later messages only got a notice that the last task's result was unknown, without the reason. When the session cannot be resumed, the next message starts a new one; when Codex fails before it starts, the service log says what it printed (with secrets masked). Exceptions: within 90 seconds after an upgrade switches over (while it can still roll back to the previous release), or when the turn combined several messages, the group is still held as before. Codex groups with Add follow-up messages to the current task turned on (the default) keep the previous behaviour in this release.

- **A message cut off by a crash is reported, not redone, and the group is not held**: When the service exits on an error nothing caught, the message it was working on gets a note in its conversation after the restart saying it was not finished (with who sent it and how it began); it is not redone and the group is not held. The session is kept, and its next turn tells the model not to continue that request unless you ask again. The group is still held when the turn combined several messages, more messages were waiting in that conversation, the executor had not yet confirmed it started, or the final reply had begun, and for a turn cut off by stopping the service yourself or by an upgrade restart.

- **Sealing a held group is no longer blocked by its own task**: When you seal a held group from Needs attention in the console, that group's own stuck turn no longer counts as another group's task, so the seal goes ahead; it still waits while other groups are running or have messages queued. Before, a group stuck after its usage limit was reached could be refused because other groups still had tasks, and had to be sealed from the command line with the service stopped.

- **A tidier console**: On the settings page, the Feishu, WeCom and Slack cards fold to one row by default (icon, name, status dot and a short summary); open one for the details, and its dot turns red when the connection fails. The interface language moves from the sidebar to a new Interface card at the top of the settings page. Version history is no longer kept in the console: Release notes → at the bottom of the Software updates card, the version badge next to the brand and the upgrade announcement in groups all link to that version's section of the release notes on the website. Chinese text left on the English interface is now in English.

- **Models chosen per group; adding a model starts with the key**: Model cards that use an API key now work like subscription cards: each group picks its model on its card under Groups · Projects or with /model, and once the card has a key, the list shows the models the provider offers right now; a group that has not chosen runs the model stored on the card. Add model asks for the API key right after the preset, and Verify key runs a short trial on the spot and says why it failed (for example the key was refused, or the endpoint does not speak the Anthropic format); the endpoint, small model, default thinking depth and the rest move under Advanced. A custom endpoint still takes its endpoint and model on the card, shared by its groups.

- **Model presets**: The preset list changes: the GLM preset moves to glm-5.3, Kimi is added and Volcano Ark is removed; the default models of the DeepSeek and MiniMax presets follow the providers' current docs as well. The MiniMax preset uses MiniMax's current endpoint, api.minimax.cn. Model cards and presets show the provider's small logo, the two subscription presets (Claude subscription and GPT via Codex) come first, and the terminal wizard's providers change to match. Existing model cards, including Volcano Ark cards and cards on the old MiniMax endpoint, are not affected and can still be used and edited.

- **Check and upgrade Claude Code**: The Claude subscription model card shows the version of the Claude Code program on this Mac and, when a newer one exists, upgrades it after you confirm: a copy installed with npm is reinstalled with npm, one from the native installer uses its own updater, and any other install is left for a manual upgrade. It will not upgrade while a group is running or queuing a Claude Code task, and every attempt is recorded in the audit log; groups that use Claude Code run the new version from their next turn.

- **The installer points to Slack first**: After the one-line install, the closing message links to connecting your project in Slack first, then notes that Feishu and WeCom are supported too, with their links.

2026-11-19

### 1.4.29 · Scheduled tasks, and a clean exit on crashes

- **Scheduled tasks**: Create, edit, pause and delete them on a conversation's console card under More settings → Scheduled tasks. There are three kinds: Model (at the time, a line marked [Scheduled] is posted and then handled like an ordinary message), Message (posts the text only) and Script (runs a command in the project folder without the model, and posts one line if it fails or times out). The time can be a cron expression, an alias such as @daily, a shorthand such as 每天 09:00, or one date and time; each task can have its own time zone. Each due time fires at most once; runs missed while the service was down, or reached more than two minutes late, are not made up; failed runs and runs with an unknown result are not retried. In this release tasks are created and changed only in the console, and WeCom conversations do not have them yet.

- **A clean exit on crashes**: When the service hits an error nothing caught, it logs the time and stack trace, stops scheduled tasks and running executors, releases its lock and removes temporary files, then exits with code 1 so the system starts it again; the cleanup waits at most 20 seconds. Before, it exited on the spot and Codex or Claude Code child processes could keep running in the background. The interrupted turn is still treated as having an unknown result after the restart.

- **Stricter proxy addresses**: In Slack setup and settings, the proxy host must be an IP address or a host name in plain ASCII: names in other scripts, labels starting with xn--, and full-width dots and digits are refused; IPv6 addresses in brackets are checked by the standard rules. Before, some of these could be saved and only failed with a different error when connecting.

- **Slack and console fixes**: In Slack, ⚠️ on a held conversation is no longer skipped when checking sealed records fails, and the failure is written to the service log; the log line for another machine connected to the same Slack app is worded more precisely. The busy follow-up switch in the console has English text: Add follow-up messages to the current task.

2026-11-19

### 1.4.28 · Slack speaks English, stopping inside a thread, a full queue no longer holds the group

- **A full queue asks you to resend instead of holding the group**: When two messages are already waiting, a new one is not handled: the bot asks you to send it again after the current task, and the running task is not affected. Before, in Feishu, WeCom and direct messages this interrupted the current task and held the whole group. A message that arrives while the current task is wrapping up is also answered with a request to resend.

- **Slack speaks English by default**: In Slack, the bot's notices, command replies, status and errors are in English, and the model is asked to answer in English (it still follows a member who writes in another language). Slack conversations that are already connected switch to English after the upgrade; for Chinese, change it on the conversation's console card under More settings → Notice language. Feishu, WeCom and local conversations are unchanged.

- **Threads in a Slack channel are handled separately**: A new @mention in the channel while a task is running no longer joins that task: it waits its turn, runs on its own and is answered in its own thread. Only a reply in the running task's thread is added to it. Replying !stop in a thread stops only that thread's task and the queue carries on; a new @bot !stop in the channel, or /sint stop, still stops the current task and clears the queue.

- **Unfinished Slack messages are marked**: After the service is killed or a conversation is sealed, messages that did not finish get ⚠️ and a single note asking you to send them again if you still need them. Deleting a queued message that has replies now cancels it as well, and several problems when the connection is renewed are fixed.

- **Slack setup: proxy, Agent option and hints**: The Slack step of the setup page fills in a terminal proxy it detects (http only); it is saved as the network proxy of the whole service, so other platforms and the local model tools use it too. Declaring the app as a Slack Agent is optional and off by default. When the bot is not in a channel, it says to /invite it first; when another machine is connected to the same Slack app, the console warns about it.

- **Wording for direct messages and one-to-one chats**: Help, status and notices name the kind of conversation: "this direct message" or "this channel" in Slack. In WeCom a one-to-one chat is no longer called a group, and its project note no longer tells you to mention the bot in a group.

- **Console fixes**: After a failed Codex upgrade the button comes back and the reason stays (local paths are masked); when a model card points to a Codex program other than the one on the PATH, the console asks for a manual upgrade instead. The number of tasks that run at once is checked against 1–32, and changing it while the service runs explains that the configuration file must be edited and the service restarted.

2026-11-18

### 1.4.27 · Confirmations in the desktop app

- **Confirmations work in the desktop app**: In the desktop app, console actions that need confirmation (full access, plain text, sealing, interrupting a task for a new session, removing a model, upgrading Codex and others) did not ask first. The console now shows its own confirmation dialog, the same in the app and in a browser: Cancel, Esc or a click outside does nothing.

2026-11-18

### 1.4.26 · Codex upgrades in the console, configuration history and stability

- **Upgrade Codex and refresh models from the console**: After a model card confirms the sign-in, the model list is read again and the card says which models were added or removed; /model in a group waits for the new list (up to 8 seconds). The Codex model card shows the version of the Codex program on this Mac and, when a newer one exists and it was installed globally with npm, upgrades it in one click. It will not upgrade while a group is running a Codex task.

- **Configuration history and restore**: The service stores a copy of the configuration when it starts and after every change in the console, keeping the latest 50. sintbot config history lists which settings each copy changed, never their values; sintbot config restore <version> puts one back while the service is stopped.

- **Steadier**: A malformed request address no longer stops the service; a Feishu request that gets no answer for 30 seconds is abandoned instead of holding the group; previews check where a file really is before serving it; a queued message reads the group's current settings when it starts; the console accepts only sensible concurrency and turn-time values; password-free access is given only to local requests that do not come through a reverse proxy.

- **Follow-ups that cite the last reply after an idle compaction (experimental)**: When Claude Code compacts its context while idle, the next turn carries the reply that was already sent, so a group message such as "1 and 3" still lands on the right items. It is kept in memory only and is gone after a restart.

2026-11-18

### 1.4.25 · A cleaner console

- **Group cards show only what works**: Cards now show only the settings this version supports: model, thinking depth, execution mode, busy follow-up, data output and plugins (view only for now). Preview, scheduled tasks, repository, design style, icons, canvas and unbind, which are not available yet, no longer appear. The Claude allowlist folds into one line and opens for editing.

- **A note when the public address is down**: If a public address is set, the console checks that it reaches this Mac. When it does not, Overview and Settings say so: Feishu sign-in from outside is unavailable for now, while the LAN console and all groups keep working.

- **Overview starts with no project selected**: Opening Overview no longer preselects a project. Click a project to see its task activity, and click it again to close it.

2026-11-16

### 1.4.24 · Slack

- **Use SintBot in Slack**: Message the bot directly, or @mention it in a channel. Answers arrive in the direct message, or in a thread under your message. It connects over Socket Mode, needs no public address and works in free workspaces.

- **Three steps, no terminal**: Choose Slack on the setup page or in console Settings: create your own app from a link that is already filled in, paste two tokens, then send the bot one message to bind the project. A token pasted in the wrong field is named at once.

- **See that it is working**: While a task runs your message shows ⏳ and a channel thread shows a Stop button; ⏳ becomes ✅ when the answer arrives. A follow-up sent during the task gets ⏳ too once it is read.

- **Commands start with !**: Slack keeps / for its own commands, so use !status, !stop, !skip, !new and !model; outside threads /sint stop works too. Images and files sent with a task are saved on your Mac for the task.

- **Create a Feishu group from the console**: Groups · Projects → Set up a group project can now create a new Feishu group and select it for binding, without creating it in Feishu first.

2026-11-14

### 1.4.23 · Smoother WeCom settings

- **WeCom card in Settings**: The WeCom card now sits below Feishu and matches its layout: connection status, bot name and bound projects up front, with the Bot ID, connection refresh and manual entry under Advanced.

- **Choose the project folder**: When adding WeCom you can browse, pick or create the project folder. A missing folder or credential is flagged at once, and the form is locked while a scan runs.

- **Consistent setup wording**: With WeCom selected, the setup steps, finished message and local-chat note describe scanning to create the bot and sending one message to bind the project.

2026-11-14

### 1.4.22 · Connect WeCom by scanning

- **Scan to create the WeCom bot**: Choose WeCom during setup, or add it from console Settings, and scan with WeCom on your phone. The bot is created and its credentials are saved on this Mac. You can still enter an existing Bot ID and Secret.

- **Start from any message**: Message the bot directly, or @mention it in a group, to bind the project. A personal organization with only you in it works through direct chat. Existing Feishu projects are kept.

- **Tasks and files in WeCom**: Use Codex or Claude Code, stop tasks, and have the assistant send project files and images back. The reply arrives when a task finishes; unknown send results are not retried automatically.

2026-11-13

### 1.4.21 · Fast for GPT groups; held groups handled in the console

- **Fast per GPT group**: Codex models gain a Speed option: Standard or Fast. Turn it on from the console group card, with /model fast in the group (/model standard to go back) or on the /model card. Changing only the speed keeps the session, works while a task is running and applies from the next message. Off by default; remembered per group and per model card; scheduled tasks always run at standard speed. It cannot be enabled for a model without a Fast tier, and switching to such a model returns to Standard with a note. The receipt states the cost: about 1.5–2x speed, quota charged at 2.5x.

- **Standard speed is now stated explicitly**: Every turn explicitly requests Standard unless the group enables Fast. When App Server reports a fallback, the card footer omits Fast. Older executors and the exec route do not report the effective tier, so their requested tier is not proof of acceleration.

- **Seal a held group from the console**: When the service is killed during a task (power loss, forced restart) and every group is held, the service still starts and the console stays available. The overview's Needs attention card and the local conversation page offer Seal and continue: the record is archived unchanged, that message is not processed again, and the service restarts by itself with a new record. Offered only when running as a managed background service; foreground runs keep the terminal steps in the guide.

- **No upgrade while the background service is disabled**: If the launchd job is disabled in the system (for example under Login Items), a console upgrade is refused with a message instead of leaving the service stopped.

- **DeepSeek preset**: Configure an API Key for DeepSeek Flash and select model and effort per project.

- **Missing-key preflight**: Missing API Keys are rejected before executor startup; keyless cards remain selectable in project settings.

2026-11-13

### 1.4.20 · Local conversations and a refined desktop interface

- **Chat directly on your Mac**: Choose a project and executor without connecting a chat platform first. Conversations stay on your Mac, and Feishu can be attached later.

- **A compact, consistent interface**: Setup and console share light and dark themes and follow the system by default. Collapsible project cards, settings navigation and responsive layouts fit narrower windows.

- **Project memory accompanies each task**: Each turn points to project convention files and available executor memory, preserving the project context.

- **Safer history and connection setup**: Recover cleanly after interrupted transcript writes. Attaching Feishu preserves local routes and history, and the package includes the complete local conversation module.

- **Compact reply cards**: Elapsed time, usage and model share one footer that wraps naturally on phones.

2026-11-12

### 1.4.18 · Browser setup and Claude idle compaction

- **Connect Feishu in the browser**: The first start opens a local setup page for project selection, phone confirmation, progress and resumable failures. Once configuration and journals are initialized, the page enters the console automatically. English and Chinese are supported.

- **Save explicit model and thinking-depth choices for new groups**: Before scanning, setup reads the selected executor's live recommended model and thinking depth and saves them for the new group. An unavailable live catalog stops setup before app creation; existing choices are preserved.

- **Safer cancellation and retries**: Cancellation stops at step boundaries. Retries reuse confirmed apps and groups, while configuration writes recheck current state to avoid overwriting another instance's setup.

- **Idle compaction for Claude groups (experimental)**: Claude Code versions advertising compact can compact an idle session after a task when context reaches half the configured compaction window. New work stops compaction first. Successful compaction and cache behavior still await real-model validation.

- **Immediate Claude quota updates from events**: Quota events from each run refresh the display promptly and reduce extra quota requests. Existing API and cache paths remain when events are unavailable.

- **Compaction exit protection and clearer setup guidance**: Unconfirmed process exit retains capacity and blocks further dispatch for that group. Configuration-file notices, language-specific guide links and startup instructions are also corrected.

2026-11-12

### 1.4.17 · Feishu scan-to-connect and third-party quotas

- **Connect Feishu with one scan**: New command sintbot connect: scan a QR code in the Feishu app to create the bot app; SintBot self-checks, opens the contact and availability scope and publishes, creates ~/Projects/<name>, creates a group with you in it, writes the configuration and initializes journals. On failure it stops at that step and tells you how to resume (--app-id, --chat); non-admins in a company organization can use --basic. The manual path remains.

- **Simpler Feishu settings**: Connection status and project groups come first. New users get a three-step scan setup guide; manual setup and app details are folded away. Console administrator sign-in is separate.

- **Third-party quota and balance**: GLM shows the 5-hour and weekly windows and falls back to the balance without a plan; MiniMax shows the 5-hour and weekly windows; DeepSeek shows the balance. Invalid credentials are shown as such; transient failures keep the last value for 10 minutes.

- **Claude subscription quota fallback**: When the Claude Code login token has expired, the CLI refreshes it itself and SintBot reads its cached quota instead of showing "unverified"; read-only, never refreshing on its own, never blocking group commands or the console.

- **Environment conflict check**: Preflight and the console model cards list environment variables and ~/.claude/settings.json or ~/.codex/config.toml settings that would reroute Claude Code or Codex; key names only, warnings only.

- **Built-in core ABI 36**: Connect decisions and wording, QR encoding, quota parsing and environment checks live in the built-in core; the core build pins its toolchain and no longer depends on the crate mirror used by the builder.

2026-11-11

### 1.4.16 · Per-group model and thinking depth

- **Choose model and depth per group**: Pick the backend, model and thinking depth on each group card in the console. Model lists come live from the local Codex and Claude Code. Subscription model cards no longer carry a model or depth; a third-party endpoint keeps its model on the model card.

- **Group command /model**: Send /model for a tap-to-pick card and confirm to apply, or send /model high, /model <model>, or /model <backend> <model> <depth>. A model or depth change on the same backend continues the conversation; a backend change starts a new one. Changes wait until the group is idle; receipts and the audit log record who made them.

- **Existing settings migrate automatically**: After the upgrade connects, each model card's model and depth move into its groups with the same effective values and no session reset, after a configuration backup. Custom Codex context windows are checked against each group's chosen model.

2026-11-11

### 1.4.15 · Simpler model settings

- **Configure the Codex context window**: Choose the executor default or a custom window on each model card. Validate known limits and distinguish requested settings from runtime reports.

- **Keep compaction settings per model**: Remove global inheritance. Choose the executor default or a custom value. Existing explicit global values become independent settings on existing models; new models use the executor default.

- **Streamline model configuration**: Group model and reasoning, context and compaction, and connection settings. Show numeric inputs only when needed and collapse capacity details. Model trials now use the model compaction setting.

2026-11-11

### 1.4.14 · Model context and per-model compaction

- **Read model context limits clearly**: Model cards distinguish known official model limits from the active executor window and usable capacity. Reported Claude windows do not replace known model limits.

- **Set compaction per model**: Configure a Codex compaction threshold or a Claude Code compaction window for each model. Models without an override retain the legacy setting; zero uses the executor’s settings. A requested value is not a confirmed trigger point.

- **Keep model details consistent**: Remove unverified compaction-point estimates and fix model-dialog refresh and English window descriptions. Installation guides explain the settings and remove a duplicated paragraph.

2026-11-10

### 1.4.13 · Reliability and task follow-up improvements

- **Restore Claude Code health information**: Visible Claude Code models show executor version and probe results. Hidden models do not trigger extra probes.

- **Retry failed upgrades safely**: Keep failed installations for inspection. Retry in a separate directory and verify before switching, without overwriting existing installations.

- **Align runtime version, model and capability information**: Each turn receives the running service version and its exact tool entry. Distinguish service, global installation and available updates; consistently resolve group model overrides and defaults.

- **Read locally retained group replies**: Look up this group’s recorded replies by source message or turn, with explicit provenance, status, truncation and retention limits. Unreadable Feishu cards are never reconstructed by guesswork.

- **Apply concurrency and maintenance checks to trials**: Allow one console trial within shared model capacity. Refuse starts during maintenance, abort and skip saving after writer loss, and retain capacity when process closure is unknown.

- **Handle early timeout callbacks**: If a timer callback arrives before the deadline, wait for the remaining interval. Abort only with elapsed-time evidence so a normal timeout is not misclassified as a fault.

- **Send console messages while a task is running**: Project messages use the same followup or queue path as group messages. The console distinguishes acceptance, waiting for the model to read, and confirmed joining; repeated submissions are deduplicated.

- **Continue output after moving a reply card**: Busy follow-ups preserve already displayed text on the relocated card, then stream subsequent output without replaying the old text. Updates arriving during the move and the final answer remain ordered.

2026-11-10

### 1.4.12 · Projects and live activity

- **Projects, concurrency and context in one panel**: Show project paths, runtime, configured reasoning and context together; restore row icon actions and display task tools, reply and compact metrics after selecting a group. Remove the top available-controls notice.

- **Actual task details and reported context**: Shows requests, follow-ups, progress, replies and the latest reported context. Reuses existing events without extra model calls; details load on demand and restored samples are labeled historical.

2026-11-10

### 1.4.11 · Unified busy follow-ups

- **Busy follow-ups default on for Codex and Claude Code**: One per-group switch preserves explicit disabling. Claude follow-ups join after confirmed reading, and continuation answers form one final reply. Recalling handed-over input cancels the whole task; uncertain delivery is never replayed.

2026-11-10

### 1.4.10 · Interrupted task completion

- **Fix: a group could stop accepting work after an executor exited mid-task**: When an accepted executor exits without a final result, the existing card shows an interruption notice. The group continues after delivery is confirmed. Partial output is not treated as an answer and the task is not automatically rerun. Check any operations already performed; uncertain closure or delivery remains held.

2026-11-10

### 1.4.9 · Failure completion and reply card improvements

- **Fix: a reply card could remain in progress after a failed task**: After a confirmed executor error and exit, the existing card shows a failure and the group can handle the next message. Without an open card, one failure notice is sent. Uncertain delivery remains held without automatic retries.

- **Improve: reply cards show the actual model and reasoning effort**: The final card shows the selected model and effort. If an unsupported effort falls back to the model default, it no longer shows that rejected effort. Long durations use minutes or hours, and absent usage no longer appears as zero tokens.

- **Fix: answers stayed at the old card position after a busy-turn follow-up**: After Codex confirms a follow-up landed, the reply card moves beneath that message. An open card is copied to the new position before the old one is recalled.

2026-11-10

### 1.4.8 · Console interjections, upgrade notices, group messaging skills

- **Fix: a message sent while the previous reply was still being delivered was refused with "wrapping up, please resend"**: A message arriving at the moment a reply, card or the stop confirmation was still on its way to Feishu used to be refused. It now waits for that delivery and is handled in arrival order; a message sent right after /stop is answered normally.
